name: The decision rests on unstructured interviews and gut judgement
what: The firm screens and chooses mainly through [conversational interviews](#term:unstructured-interview) and the hiring manager's impression. Unstructured interviews predict job performance at .19 against .42 for structured ones [1](#cite:1), and adding unstructured interview ratings to valid test scores lowers decision accuracy while raising confidence [9](#cite:9). Interviewers form confident impressions even from random answers and cannot tell random interviews from real ones [8](#cite:8).
mechanism: Two mechanisms keep the method alive: sensemaking, by which an interviewer builds a coherent story from almost anything, and dilution, by which weak information crowds out strong [8](#cite:8). Combining information by judgement rather than by formula costs more than a third of the achievable validity (r .28 vs .44) [7](#cite:7), and managers who override a test on their own read of the candidate hire worse on average [10](#cite:10). Practitioners also disbelieve the evidence: HR professionals place far less faith in tests than the research supports [20](#cite:20), and structure is resisted by interviewers who were never trained in it [19](#cite:19).
how_to_tell: Interviewers ask different questions of different candidates and there is no written rating scale (the defining absence of structure [41](#cite:41) [6](#cite:6)).
Decisions are explained in terms of fit or feel rather than scored evidence ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
A candidate who scored well on a [work sample](#term:work-sample-test) or test was rejected after an interview with no documented reason (the override pattern in [10](#cite:10)).

name: The first screen rejects qualified people on proxies
what: Résumé and applicant-tracking screens built on exact-match criteria (a degree, a title, years in a role, an unbroken work history) reject candidates who could do the job. In the Harvard Business School and Accenture survey behind the "hidden workers" report, 88 percent of employers said qualified high-skilled candidates were rejected outright for not matching criteria exactly, and 94 percent said so for middle-skilled candidates [44](#cite:44). The proxies are weak predictors: years of job experience carries an [operational validity](#term:operational-validity) of .07 [1](#cite:1).
mechanism: A screen is only as valid as the criteria it encodes, and the convenient criteria are the least predictive. [Knowledge tests](#term:job-knowledge-test) (.40) and [work samples](#term:work-sample-test) (.33) predict performance; experience-years (.07) barely does [1](#cite:1). Negative filters that remove anyone missing a token therefore discard signal; the report's remedy is affirmative filters that search for required skills [44](#cite:44). Where the screen is automated, the same logic exposes the firm to [adverse-impact](#term:adverse-impact) liability (see c-algorithmic-screen-exposure).
how_to_tell: The posting lists a degree or a years-of-experience threshold that was never tied to a [job analysis](#term:job-analysis) (what [29 CFR 1607](#term:uniform-guidelines).5 asks for [32](#cite:32)).
Many applicants, few passed to interview, and the rejections are keyword or threshold mismatches rather than scored assessments ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
Hires who did well came through a [referral](#term:referral-hiring) or a manual exception rather than the screen (synthesis).

name: The selection criteria have never been validated or documented
what: The firm cannot show that its screens, tests and interview questions relate to the job. The [Uniform Guidelines](#term:uniform-guidelines) accept criterion-related, content or construct validity evidence tied to important elements of job performance [32](#cite:32), expect records of selection rates by sex and by race or ethnic group [31](#cite:31), and require more evidence for ranking than for pass/fail use where ranking has more [adverse impact](#term:adverse-impact) [32](#cite:32). The employer remains responsible even when a vendor supplied the tool [33](#cite:33).
mechanism: Under Title VII a neutral procedure that disproportionately excludes a protected group must be job-related and consistent with business necessity, and a challenger may point to a less discriminatory alternative [33](#cite:33). Without documented validation the firm has no answer to a four-fifths-rule finding [31](#cite:31), and professional practice (the SIOP Principles, adopted as APA policy in 2018) sets the bar for what "validated" means [29](#cite:29). Small firms rarely have this evidence, which is also why they default to judgement (c-unstructured-judgement) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to_tell: No [job analysis](#term:job-analysis) exists for the opening; the criteria were copied from an earlier posting (synthesis).
Selection rates by group are not recorded, so the [four-fifths](#term:four-fifths-rule) test cannot be run [31](#cite:31).
A vendor assessment is used on the vendor's word about validity [33](#cite:33).

name: Slow decisions and slow offers lose candidates
what: Candidates leave while the firm deliberates. In the one field study of offer timing (N = 3,012 at one company), earlier post-interview offers were more likely to be accepted by both student and experienced candidates, and hires made on fast offers performed and stayed no differently [15](#cite:15). Favourable perceptions of the process predict [offer-acceptance](#term:offer-acceptance-rate) intentions [14](#cite:14). In 2025, 41 percent of organisations reported rising [candidate ghosting](#term:candidate-ghosting) and the median [time-to-fill](#term:time-to-fill) was about 45 days [43](#cite:43).
mechanism: Applicants read speed as interest and delay as disinterest or disorganisation, and act on competing offers meanwhile [15](#cite:15) [14](#cite:14). Where approvals sit with busy managers or an outside authority, the firm's cycle time is set by the slowest signature ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker); the customer-approval case is recorded in sweep 7).
how_to_tell: Days between final interview and offer exceed the firm's own stated target, or no target exists (synthesis).
Candidates withdraw after interviewing well, citing another offer (the competing-offer correlate of withdrawal in [16](#cite:16)).

name: A long, repetitive or opaque process drives withdrawal
what: Candidates drop out of multi-stage processes for reasons the firm can see and reasons it cannot. Among 3,550 police applicants, those who withdrew differed from those who stayed on their perceptions of the organisation and the process, career commitment, current employment, relocation and the views of family and friends, and early and late withdrawers differed [16](#cite:16). Perceptions of procedural justice and of a procedure's face validity predict attraction and acceptance intentions [14](#cite:14). Developers describe [technical interviews](#term:technical-interview) as time-consuming, anxiety-provoking and governed by unwritten norms [22](#cite:22).
mechanism: Each added stage is a fresh chance to form a negative perception and a fresh demand on the candidate's time, and candidates with alternatives need the least provocation to leave [16](#cite:16) [14](#cite:14). No primary study of the number of interview rounds against withdrawal was found in this sweep; the vendor figures circulating on that point are not carried ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker); see queries).
how_to_tell: Withdrawals cluster at a particular stage rather than spreading evenly (the stage-specific pattern in [16](#cite:16)).
Candidates are not told at first contact how many steps there are or how long they take (synthesis).
Several interviewers ask the same questions because no interview plan assigns competencies to interviews (synthesis).

name: The technical interview measures anxiety as much as skill
what: [Live coding](#term:technical-interview) on a whiteboard while being watched is the standard technical interview, and in a [randomised trial](#term:field-experiment) of 48 computer-science students it halved performance on the same problem relative to solving it privately, while raising measured stress and cognitive load [21](#cite:21). Practitioners on a large developer forum describe the format as unrelated to real work, biased toward the young and recently drilled, time-consuming and anxiety-provoking [22](#cite:22).
mechanism: Being observed and narrating one's reasoning loads working memory and triggers evaluation anxiety, so the score mixes problem-solving ability with stress tolerance that the job may not require [21](#cite:21). The format also screens on preparation for the format itself ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker) from [22](#cite:22)). [Work samples](#term:work-sample-test) that resemble the job remain valid predictors (.33) when built from a [job analysis](#term:job-analysis) and scored consistently [1](#cite:1) [17](#cite:17).
how_to_tell: The technical exercise is a puzzle the role never poses, rather than a sample of its actual work (the relevance complaint in [22](#cite:22)).
Strong candidates on take-home or portfolio evidence fail the live exercise (synthesis).

name: The most valid tests show the largest group differences
what: [Cognitive ability tests](#term:cognitive-ability-test) carry a Black–White [standardised difference](#term:subgroup-difference) of .79, [work samples](#term:work-sample-test) .67, [job knowledge tests](#term:job-knowledge-test) .54, [structured interviews](#term:structured-interview) .23 and [integrity tests](#term:integrity-test) .10, so the choice of predictor sets the [adverse-impact](#term:adverse-impact) exposure as well as the validity [1](#cite:1). Corrected for the [range restriction](#term:range-restriction) of using an interview as a first screen, two behavioural interviews showed d of .36 and .56 [18](#cite:18). A selection rate below [four-fifths](#term:four-fifths-rule) of the highest group's generally indicates adverse impact under the [Uniform Guidelines](#term:uniform-guidelines) [31](#cite:31).
mechanism: Validity and subgroup difference travel together for cognitively loaded measures; the reviewed remedies are simulations with low cognitive load and high fidelity, alternative cognitive measures and Pareto-optimal predictor weighting, with banding controversial and coaching of small effect [25](#cite:25). The trade-off is real but not automatic: when a national retailer replaced informal screening with a standardised test across 1,363 stores, minority hiring did not fall and the tenure gains spread evenly across groups, because the informal screen it replaced was no less biased [11](#cite:11).
how_to_tell: A cognitively loaded test is used for ranking rather than pass/fail, which the Uniform Guidelines treat as needing more validity evidence [32](#cite:32).
Selection rates by group are not tracked, so the trade-off is invisible until a complaint ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

name: An automated or AI screen carries liability and notice duties the firm has not met
what: An [algorithmic tool](#term:algorithmic-screening) used to make or inform a selection decision is a selection procedure under the [Uniform Guidelines](#term:uniform-guidelines), the employer is liable for a vendor's tool, and the [four-fifths rule](#term:four-fifths-rule) is a rule of thumb rather than a safe harbour, as the EEOC stated in May 2023 before withdrawing the document on January 27, 2025 [35](#cite:35) [36](#cite:36). States now carry the duty: Illinois bars discriminatory AI use and requires notice from January 1, 2026 [38](#cite:38); New York City requires an annual bias audit, a published summary and candidate notice, with penalties of \$500–\$1,500 a day [37](#cite:37); California's regulations effective October 1, 2025 define [automated-decision systems](#term:automated-employment-decision-tool), extend liability to agents, treat anti-bias testing as a defence factor and require four-year [record retention](#term:applicant-record-retention) [40](#cite:40); Colorado's act was delayed to June 30, 2026 [39](#cite:39).
mechanism: The statutes do not change the Title VII test; they add notice, audit and retention duties and make the vendor's tool the employer's problem [35](#cite:35) [40](#cite:40). A screen can be built to reduce [subgroup differences](#term:subgroup-difference) while adding validity, as NLP scoring of narrative applications did in four Air Force samples (N = 1,828) [23](#cite:23), which is what the regulations now expect an employer to be able to show. Enforcement so far has been thin: New York City's agency received two complaints in two years and its own review missed most of what the state auditors found [37](#cite:37).
how_to_tell: A vendor screen ranks or rejects applicants and the firm cannot say what it scores or whether it was tested for selection-rate differences [35](#cite:35).
Candidates in Illinois, New York City or California were not notified that an automated tool was used [37](#cite:37) [38](#cite:38) [40](#cite:40).
ADS records are not retained (four years in California) [40](#cite:40).

name: The firm asks for what the law reserves until after a conditional offer
what: Three sequencing rules bind the interview and application. Under the ADA, [disability-related questions](#term:pre-employment-inquiry) and medical examinations are barred before a conditional offer, and after it they must be asked of everyone entering the job category [34](#cite:34) [33](#cite:33). Under the federal [Fair Chance Act](#term:fair-chance-act), a contractor may not ask about criminal history for positions under a federal contract until after a conditional offer, with exceptions for classified-access and national-security positions [48](#cite:48); the EEOC separately treats arrest-only exclusions as not job-related and asks for targeted screens with individualised assessment [47](#cite:47). Under 8 U.S.C. 1324b, a posting for ITAR- or [EAR-controlled](#term:ear) work may not be limited to U.S. citizens, or to citizens and permanent residents, because the export rules admit U.S. nationals, refugees and asylees; settlements ran from \$365,000 to \$500,000 per employer in 2023 [49](#cite:49) [50](#cite:50) [51](#cite:51).
mechanism: Each rule pushes a legitimate question to a later point in the sequence or narrows how it may be phrased, and each has been enforced against employers who were trying to comply with a different rule (export control, security requirements) [49](#cite:49) [47](#cite:47). The common failure is a job ad or application form written for convenience rather than for the sequence ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to_tell: The application asks about health, accommodation needs beyond the hiring process, or criminal history before an offer [34](#cite:34) [48](#cite:48).
The posting says "U.S. citizens only" or "must be a U.S. citizen or green-card holder" for export-controlled work [49](#cite:49) [50](#cite:50).
Export screening is done through the [Form I-9](#term:form-i-9) or dictates which I-9 documents to present [51](#cite:51).

name: Too few qualified candidates within reach
what: The local market does not hold enough people with the skills the opening needs. Among small-business owners hiring or trying to hire in September 2026, 87 percent reported few or no qualified applicants, and 32 percent of all owners had unfilled openings [71](#cite:71). Computer and IT occupations are projected to generate about 280,000 openings a year through 2035 at a median wage of \$109,470 [84](#cite:84). Reach by relocation has shrunk: 1.6 percent of job seekers moved for a job in early 2023, against 7.7 percent in late 2018 [85](#cite:85), while workers value a hybrid option at a mean 8 percent of pay and half of surveyed firms expanded remote work to hold staff and moderate wage growth [70](#cite:70).
mechanism: Supply is set by the occupation's size and the firm's geographic reach, and the second has changed character: candidates who once relocated now expect to stay put and work remotely or hybrid [85](#cite:85) [70](#cite:70) [69](#cite:69). A firm that must have people onsite, or [cleared](#term:security-clearance), competes for the local pool against employers who can offer the 8 percent differential in kind ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)). Who applies at all is partly self-selection: the conscientious and extraverted are more easily attracted, the high-GPA less so [82](#cite:82).
how_to_tell: Postings draw few applicants who meet the basic qualifications even after the screen is corrected (see c-keyword-screen-rejects-qualified) (synthesis).

The role requires onsite presence or a clearance and the posting offers neither remote work nor a relocation package (the two reach [levers](#term:lever-record) in [70](#cite:70) [85](#cite:85)) (synthesis).

name: The posting draws volume without fit
what: The ad produces applicants who do not match the job, or too few who do. What a posting draws is governed by its title and its pay figure: across titles, higher-paying postings draw fewer applicants because the titles are senior, while within a title a 10 percent higher posted wage draws 7.7 percent more applicants [65](#cite:65). By May 2025, 59 percent of US postings and 63 percent of software-development postings on the largest job board carried a salary figure [75](#cite:75). Half of organisations report too few applicants [43](#cite:43).
mechanism: Applicants sort on the words and the number before they sort on anything else [65](#cite:65); a vague title or a missing range sends the posting to the wrong queue or to none. Attraction then runs through what the job and the organisation are, how the process feels and whether the applicant expects to be hired [63](#cite:63). [Masculine-coded wording](#term:gendered-wording) lowers the appeal and the sense of belonging for women without changing what they think the job requires [77](#cite:77) (see c-ad-wording-and-targeting-exclude).
how_to_tell: The title is internal jargon or a level code rather than the name candidates search for (the title effect in [65](#cite:65)) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
No pay range is shown where competitors show one [75](#cite:75); a range is required by law in the posting state (see pay-transparency-posting-laws).
Applicant volume is high but the share meeting basic qualifications is low (synthesis).

name: The firm cannot tell which channel produces hires who stay
what: Spending goes to the same job boards and agencies without a record of which source produced qualified candidates, starts and retained employees. The evidence says sources differ: inside sources ([referrals](#term:referral-hiring), rehires, internal transfers) show higher tenure, less turnover and better performance than outside ones [62](#cite:62), and referred hires quit 10 to 30 percent less [60](#cite:60). Until October 26, 2026, federal contractors were required to log online expressions of interest, search criteria and dates under the [Internet Applicant rule](#term:executive-order-11246) [87](#cite:87), which the EO 11246 rescission removes with part 60-1 [86](#cite:86).
mechanism: Source effects run through accurate expectations: inside recruits know what they are joining [62](#cite:62). Without a per-source record of qualified-rate, start-rate and 90-day retention the firm cannot see the difference and keeps buying volume ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)). The [Uniform Guidelines](#term:uniform-guidelines)' selection-rate records by group remain required and are the natural place to add source [31](#cite:31).
how_to_tell: Source of hire is not recorded, or is recorded only as "job board" (synthesis).
Agency and board spend is renewed on volume rather than on hires who passed probation (synthesis).

name: The referral network is narrow and reproduces itself
what: [Referrals](#term:referral-hiring) are the best-evidenced source: referred applicants are more likely to be interviewed and hired, and referred workers are about 15 percent less likely to leave in a financial-services firm [61](#cite:61) and 10 to 30 percent less likely to quit across nine firms in three industries [60](#cite:60). The same mechanism narrows the pool: referral networks are segregated, firms hire and retain people who resemble the founders' networks, and the effect fades only as cumulative hires grow [81](#cite:81). A firm whose employees' networks are small, or all alike, gets few referrals and the same kind each time ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
mechanism: Employees refer people they know, who are like them [81](#cite:81); referrers with above-median productivity produce referrals worth four times those from below-median referrers [60](#cite:60). The 101-study literature models referrer motives, the process and outcomes for both parties [67](#cite:67).
how_to_tell: Referrals come from the same few employees (the referrer-quality effect in [60](#cite:60)) (synthesis).
New hires resemble the existing staff on school, employer or background (the composition mechanism in [81](#cite:81)) (synthesis).

name: Candidates do not know the firm, or know it unfavourably
what: A small firm competes on an image candidates may not hold. Favourable [employer images](#term:employer-image) relate to better recruitment outcomes and are formed by recruiters and by word of mouth [64](#cite:64); job and organisation characteristics, recruiter behaviour, process perceptions, fit and hiring expectancy predict attraction, while recruiter demographics do not [63](#cite:63). Half of organisations report losing talent to competitors [43](#cite:43).
mechanism: Image works through what applicants believe the job and the organisation are and whether they see a fit [63](#cite:63) [62](#cite:62); a firm without a public footprint is judged on the recruiter and the posting alone ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)). The widely circulated figures on review-site ratings rest on a working paper that was withdrawn and is not carried.
how_to_tell: Candidates cannot say what the firm does or why it is different before the first interview (synthesis).
Offers are declined for named competitors the firm never positioned itself against (synthesis).

name: The ad's words and its delivery exclude people the firm wants
what: Three things in and around the ad shrink the pool without anyone deciding to. [Masculine-coded wording](#term:gendered-wording) appears in 97 percent of professional ads for male-dominated jobs and lowers women's appeal and belonging ratings for the same job [77](#cite:77). Algorithmic ad delivery showed a gender-neutral STEM ad to fewer women because they are a more expensive audience [66](#cite:66). And the law bars some words outright: "young", "college student" and "recent college graduate" indicate an unlawful age preference [78](#cite:78), and "U.S. citizens only" on export-controlled work has drawn settlements of \$365,000 to \$500,000 [49](#cite:49) [50](#cite:50).
mechanism: Wording signals who belongs and lowers appeal through belonging, not through perceived skill [77](#cite:77); cost-optimising delivery crowds out expensive audiences [66](#cite:66); the statutory terms are strict liability in the ad itself [78](#cite:78) [49](#cite:49).
how_to_tell: The ad contains the listed age terms or a citizenship restriction [78](#cite:78) [49](#cite:49).
The applicant pool is less diverse than the occupation (the signal in [77](#cite:77) [66](#cite:66)) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).

name: A degree or years-of-experience requirement shrinks the pool for little validity
what: The posting demands a credential the job does not need. Roles dropping [degree requirements](#term:degree-requirement) rose almost fourfold from 2014 to 2023, yet non-degree hiring in those roles rose only 3.5 percentage points and the economy-wide effect was less than one hire in 700; the non-degree hires who were made stayed longer [68](#cite:68) [58](#cite:58). Nearly 70 percent of campus-recruiting employers say they use [skills-based hiring](#term:skills-based-hiring) [79](#cite:79). Years of job experience predicts performance at .07 and years of education was excluded for insufficient data in the 2022 re-estimation [1](#cite:1).
mechanism: The requirement in the ad becomes the criterion in the screen (c-keyword-screen-rejects-qualified), so removing it from the posting changes nothing unless the screen changes too, which is why announced removals produced so little hiring change [68](#cite:68). The pool narrows on a proxy with almost no validity [1](#cite:1).
how_to_tell: The posting requires a bachelor's degree or N years for a role whose [job analysis](#term:job-analysis) names skills, not credentials ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
The firm announced skills-based hiring but the ATS still filters on degree (the "in name only" group in [68](#cite:68)).

name: The cleared pool is closed and expensive
what: An already-cleared hire can only come from someone another [sponsor](#term:clearance-sponsorship) [cleared](#term:security-clearance): no individual can initiate a clearance, only a sponsoring agency can [80](#cite:80). The last public count put about 4.2 million [clearance holders](#term:cleared-population) in October 2019, 1.35 million of them contractors or other, 672,656 at [top secret](#term:top-secret) [80](#cite:80). Cleared professionals averaged \$119,131 in total compensation in the 2024 survey, 13 percent had switched employers for pay in the past year, and a [Secret clearance](#term:secret) was worth about \$9,500 over Confidential, Top Secret about \$23,800 over Secret [89](#cite:89). A vendor survey put cleared IT [time-to-fill](#term:time-to-fill) at 41 to 60 days [88](#cite:88).
mechanism: The pool is fixed in the short run by prior sponsorship and shrinks with every departure from the cleared workforce; firms compete for the same people with pay [89](#cite:89) and with the few channels that reach them ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)). Sponsoring a new clearance moves the problem to the clear-and-start stage, where [investigation inventory](#term:investigation-inventory) and [timeliness](#term:end-to-end-timeliness) decide (sweep 4) [54](#cite:54) [56](#cite:56).
how_to_tell: The posting requires an active clearance at a level the local market rarely holds (synthesis).
Offers lose to pay; the clearance premium in [89](#cite:89) is the competitor's bid (synthesis).
conflicts: The clearance population figure is from October 2019 [80](#cite:80); no newer public count was found. The cleared time-to-fill rests on a 2021 vendor survey of unstated size [88](#cite:88).

name: The salary the market expects exceeds what the contract rate can carry
what: Under a [time-and-materials](#term:time-and-materials-contract) or labor-hour contract each [labor category](#term:labor-category) has a fixed hourly rate that already contains the wage, [overhead](#term:overhead-rate), [general and administrative expense](#term:general-and-administrative-rate) and profit [98](#cite:98), so the salary the firm can pay is what remains after its indirect rates and margin come out of that rate ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)). Market pay has been rising 3.1 percent a year in wages and 3.3 percent in total compensation [103](#cite:103); software developers averaged \$148,100 in May 2025 [110](#cite:110); [cleared professionals](#term:cleared-population) averaged \$119,131, with a [Secret clearance](#term:secret) worth about \$9,500 over Confidential and a [Top Secret](#term:top-secret) about \$23,800 over Secret [89](#cite:89). Under cost-type contracts the salary must also be reasonable by comparison with similar firms and conform to an established plan [100](#cite:100).
mechanism: The rate is set at award and moves only through the contract's price-adjustment mechanism, which on GSA schedules allows three increases a period inside a request window and needs approval beyond ten percent [117](#cite:117); the market moves every month [103](#cite:103). Hours worked by someone who does not meet the category's qualifications are not payable at all [99](#cite:99), so the firm cannot bill a higher-category rate for a lower-category person to close the gap (synthesis). The [compensation cap](#term:compensation-cap) (\$671,000 for 2025 by the accounting-firm figure) does not bind technical hires at this level [107](#cite:107).
how_to_tell: Offers at the market median exceed the [wrap-rate](#term:wrap-rate) arithmetic for the labor category (synthesis from [98](#cite:98) [110](#cite:110)).
Candidates decline on pay and the firm cannot move without a rate change (the price-adjustment window in [117](#cite:117)).
conflicts: The cap figure rests on an accounting firm's page [107](#cite:107); the OFPP determination was not found (todo).

name: Contract rates escalate slower than the labor market
what: A labor rate fixed at award and escalated by the contract's own schedule falls behind a market in which wages rose 3.1 percent and benefits 3.8 percent in the year to June 2026 [103](#cite:103). On GSA schedules a contractor may request at most three price increases a contract period, only inside a window, thirty days apart, with contracting-officer approval beyond ten percent [117](#cite:117). Service-contract [wage determinations](#term:wage-determination) and the \$5.55 [health-and-welfare rate](#term:health-and-welfare-rate) set floors that move on the Department of Labor's calendar, not the firm's [101](#cite:101).
mechanism: Fixed rates are the price the customer agreed to; relief comes only through the adjustment clause, a modification, or repricing at option or [recompete](#term:recompete) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker) from [117](#cite:117) [98](#cite:98)). The evidence a firm can bring to that conversation is market escalation [103](#cite:103), awarded ceiling rates for comparable categories [111](#cite:111), and its own recruiting and retention record (synthesis).
how_to_tell: The category rate has not moved in two or more years while the [ECI](#term:employment-cost-index) has [103](#cite:103).
CALC+ ceiling rates for the same category, education and [clearance](#term:security-clearance) sit above the firm's awarded rate [111](#cite:111).

name: Larger employers offer more total compensation than the salary comparison shows
what: Benefits are thirty percent of private-industry compensation cost and 31.5 percent for management and professional occupations [104](#cite:104); a family health premium averaged \$26,993 in 2025, and 97 percent of firms with 200 or more workers offer coverage against 59 percent of smaller firms [105](#cite:105). Working conditions are a central part of compensation in their own right [94](#cite:94): workers value the option to work from home at about 8 percent of wages and would give up about 20 percent to avoid employer-set, short-notice schedules [115](#cite:115). Cross-firm pay transparency moves workers toward higher-paying firms and sharpens competition [91](#cite:91); half of organisations report losing talent to competitors [43](#cite:43).
mechanism: Candidates compare total packages and arrangements, not base pay alone [94](#cite:94) [115](#cite:115); a small firm's genuine advantages (scope, access, flexibility, growth) are real compensation when they are stated and priced, and invisible when they are not ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)). A material base-pay gap is not offset by the rest: job and organisation characteristics predict attraction and choice [63](#cite:63).
how_to_tell: Offers are declined for employers whose benefits or arrangements the firm did not compare against (synthesis).
The offer letter states base pay only (synthesis from [104](#cite:104)).

name: A market-rate offer puts the new hire above the people already doing the job
what: External hires into comparable jobs started about 18 percent higher than internal promotees in a financial-services firm, performed worse for two years and left more often [93](#cite:93). When employees learn what peers earn, those below their unit's median lose satisfaction and search for other jobs while those above gain nothing [92](#cite:92). Under state right-to-discuss laws wages run about 2 percent lower as employers hold the line to avoid renegotiating with everyone [90](#cite:90). The [Equal Pay Act](#term:equal-pay-act) requires equal pay for substantially equal work in the same establishment and forbids cutting anyone's pay to close a gap [112](#cite:112); in the Ninth Circuit prior salary cannot justify a differential at all [116](#cite:116).
mechanism: The new offer becomes the comparison point for every incumbent in the same job, and the response is asymmetric: the underpaid react, the overpaid do not [92](#cite:92). The firm then either raises incumbents (a recurring cost) or accepts the turnover risk, and the law closes the third option of lowering anyone [112](#cite:112) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to_tell: The proposed offer exceeds what incumbents in the same job earn (the comparison in [93](#cite:93)).
Incumbents can see or discuss pay ([posting laws](#term:pay-range-posting-law); right-to-discuss protections) [90](#cite:90) [76](#cite:76).

name: The way the offer is made creates legal exposure or a gap the firm did not intend
what: Roughly twenty states and several localities bar asking about salary history, some bar even confirming it until an offer is out [106](#cite:106); the early bans raised women's earnings relative to men's by about 1 percent, mainly among job changers [96](#cite:96). When a posting says nothing about negotiability, men negotiate more than women; when it says pay is negotiable the gap disappears or reverses [95](#cite:95). Under the [Equal Pay Act](#term:equal-pay-act) a differential must rest on seniority, merit, production or a job-related factor, and the employer carries the burden [112](#cite:112). A sign-on or [retention bonus](#term:retention-bonus) is [allowable](#term:allowable-cost) on a cost-type contract only under a plan or agreement that existed before the services, and major plan changes need the administrative contracting officer's review [100](#cite:100).
mechanism: Each rule removes an anchor or an ambiguity the offer process used to lean on: prior pay as the anchor [106](#cite:106) [116](#cite:116), silence on negotiation as the default [95](#cite:95), and ad hoc bonuses as the closer [100](#cite:100). The firm that does not replace them with a stated range and a plan drifts into differentials it cannot defend ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to_tell: The application or interview asks for current or prior pay [106](#cite:106).
Offers vary by candidate without a documented job-related reason [112](#cite:112).
A bonus is promised in an offer letter with no written plan behind it [100](#cite:100).

name: Accepted candidates withdraw or take a counteroffer before they start
what: An accepted offer is not a start. Earlier offers were more often accepted, with no later penalty [15](#cite:15); process perceptions predict acceptance intentions [14](#cite:14); 13 percent of [cleared professionals](#term:cleared-population) switched employers for pay in the past year [89](#cite:89); 41 percent of organisations report rising [candidate ghosting](#term:candidate-ghosting) [43](#cite:43). In a staffing firm's survey of 5,500 managers, 58 percent extend [counteroffers](#term:counteroffer) and those who accept one stay a mean 1.7 years [113](#cite:113). Four in five organisations pay [sign-on bonuses](#term:signing-bonus) and one in eight evaluates whether they work [118](#cite:118).
mechanism: Between acceptance and start the candidate still holds options and the current employer still holds a counter; the firm's [levers](#term:lever-record) are speed, contact and a package the candidate can compare [15](#cite:15) [14](#cite:14) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)). No peer-reviewed study of counteroffer outcomes was found; the staffing-firm figure is carried as [survey-grade](#term:practitioner-survey) [113](#cite:113).
how_to_tell: Weeks pass between acceptance and start with no contact (synthesis from [15](#cite:15)).
Withdrawals cite a counteroffer or a competing total package (the comparison in [104](#cite:104) [105](#cite:105)) (synthesis).

name: The offer depends on an award the firm does not control
what: A candidate named as [key personnel](#term:key-personnel-clause) in a proposal is hired only if the proposal wins. At GAO, an offeror that knows a proposed key person has become unavailable must tell the agency, and the proposal is then unacceptable unless discussions are reopened; the duty binds protesters as well as awardees [108](#cite:108). The Court of Federal Claims declined to impose that duty absent a solicitation term, requiring only a reasonable belief at submission that the person would be available [109](#cite:109). Either way the firm cannot promise a start date, and the candidate cannot wait indefinitely ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker); the candidate side is sweep 4).
mechanism: The proposal commits a named person to a start the customer sets; the person's availability is a condition of the proposal's acceptability [108](#cite:108) [114](#cite:114); the firm's exposure runs both ways: lose the person and the award is at risk, keep the person waiting and the person leaves (synthesis).
how_to_tell: The offer letter is contingent on contract award with no date (synthesis).
The solicitation names the position as key personnel and the proposal carries the candidate's résumé [108](#cite:108).
conflicts: GAO [108](#cite:108) and the Court of Federal Claims [109](#cite:109) disagree on whether a freestanding duty to notify exists; the solicitation's terms decide in practice.

name: The firm can sponsor a clearance only for a contract it already has
what: An uncleared candidate can be [cleared](#term:security-clearance) only on the firm's request, and the firm may request eligibility only for an employee whose access is essential to a classified contract, for the minimum number of people, never to build a cache of cleared staff [119](#cite:119). The request also needs a [facility clearance](#term:facility-clearance) the firm cannot apply for itself: a contracting activity or a cleared [prime](#term:prime-contractor) has to [sponsor](#term:clearance-sponsorship) it on a bona fide requirement, and the firm's senior official, security officer and insider-threat official must be cleared first [120](#cite:120) [146](#cite:146). A [requisition](#term:requisition) that reads "active clearance required" is therefore often the only lawful shape for an opening with no DD 254 behind it, and it draws from a pool of about 1.35 million cleared contractor and other personnel on the last public count [80](#cite:80).
mechanism: Eligibility is tied to a need the government recognises, not to the firm's wish to be ready [119](#cite:119); a candidate cannot start a clearance alone [80](#cite:80); the facility clearance is itself sponsored and takes its own course through NISS and the key officials' investigations [146](#cite:146). Without the contract there is no request, without the request no clock, and the opening can be filled only by someone already eligible ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to_tell: There is no DD 254 or pre-award authorization for the opening, so there is nothing to sponsor against [146](#cite:146).
The firm holds no entity eligibility determination, or its FSO cannot name the sponsor [120](#cite:120).
The requisition says "must hold" rather than "must obtain" and the pool is thin [80](#cite:80) (synthesis).

name: The clearance takes longer than the opening can wait
what: An industry [Secret](#term:secret) took 197 days from initiation to adjudication in the third quarter of FY2026 and a [Top Secret](#term:top-secret) 243, with adjudication now the longest phase, on [DCSA](#term:dcsa)'s new all-cases basis [126](#cite:126) [125](#cite:125); the government's own targets are 40 days for a moderate-risk and 75 for a high-risk position [54](#cite:54). The [investigation inventory](#term:investigation-inventory) rose again in the same quarter [54](#cite:54), and GAO found that the published [timeliness](#term:end-to-end-timeliness) statistics had understated the real figures from 2020 to 2024 [56](#cite:56). Against that, the median [time to fill](#term:time-to-fill) a role is about 45 days [43](#cite:43), and a pre-employment investigation requires the hire to start within 45 days of the grant [119](#cite:119). A [temporary eligibility](#term:temporary-eligibility) can bridge the gap when nothing adverse surfaces [119](#cite:119), but no public figure says how often a contractor applicant gets one or how long it takes [127](#cite:127).
mechanism: The firm does not run the clock: initiation is the only phase it influences (20 to 21 days of the total [126](#cite:126)); the investigation and the adjudication belong to DCSA and the adjudicative facility [119](#cite:119) [126](#cite:126). A hire who cannot be [cleared](#term:security-clearance) before the work starts either waits unpaid, waits on the firm's payroll, or leaves ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker); see c-long-interval-loses-accepted-hires and c-no-chargeable-work-before-access).
how_to_tell: The candidate has no current eligibility and the start date is inside the current DCSA end-to-end figure [126](#cite:126).
The customer will not accept an interim, or the work needs RD, COMSEC, NATO, [SCI](#term:sensitive-compartmented-information) or SAP access that an interim does not reach [119](#cite:119).
The offer letter names a start date the firm has not derived from the clearance clock (synthesis).
conflicts: The PAC quarterly reports government-wide figures far below DCSA's industry figures and on a basis that changed in FY2026 Q3 [54](#cite:54) [126](#cite:126); the industry figures are carried from a vendor report of the NISPPAC slides because the slide text could not be read cleanly [125](#cite:125).

name: Eligibility is not access to the site, the network or the program
what: A favourable eligibility determination lets the firm grant access to classified information; it does not by itself put the hire at a desk. A [Common Access Card](#term:common-access-card) needs a government [sponsor](#term:clearance-sponsorship) and is issued, even on an [interim](#term:temporary-eligibility) basis, only after a favourable fingerprint check with an investigation already submitted [138](#cite:138) [137](#cite:137); an interim card does not transfer between sponsors [137](#cite:137). A [clearance](#term:security-clearance) held elsewhere moves by [reciprocity](#term:reciprocity), which the rule says takes five business days [122](#cite:122) and which agencies do not reliably track, with contractors telling GAO they hear nothing while they wait [145](#cite:145). [SCI](#term:sensitive-compartmented-information) and SAP access on a temporary basis is a separate decision of the granting authority [119](#cite:119), a [polygraph](#term:polygraph) is scheduled only after a preliminary determination [122](#cite:122) and is lawful for defence and intelligence contractor staff [147](#cite:147), and a cyber work role requires the [foundational qualification](#term:dod-8140) on the day the work starts [139](#cite:139). At DHS the interval from a favourable determination to [onboarding](#term:onboarding) ran 41 days in FY2026 Q3 [125](#cite:125).
mechanism: Each access is a separate decision by a separate owner with its own prerequisite: the credential needs the investigation, the account needs the credential, the program needs the read-in, the role needs the certificate [137](#cite:137) [138](#cite:138) [139](#cite:139) [119](#cite:119). None of the owners is the firm, and the rules give the firm no standing to speed them ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to_tell: The hire holds eligibility but no sponsor has registered a CAC request, or the fingerprint results are outstanding [138](#cite:138).
The position needs SCI, SAP or a polygraph the candidate does not already hold [119](#cite:119) [122](#cite:122).
The role is a cyberspace work role and the candidate lacks the foundational certification [139](#cite:139).
The reciprocity request has passed five business days without a decision [122](#cite:122) [145](#cite:145).

name: The longer the wait between acceptance and start, the more accepted hires never start
what: Among 157,154 accepted entry-level offers at one employer, 4.1 percent of hires never showed up, and each additional week between acceptance and the start date raised the odds of a [no-show](#term:new-hire-no-show) by about a fifth (OR 1.22) [144](#cite:144). The people who disappeared mostly took another job (39 percent) or cited pay (29 percent); a [referral](#term:referral-hiring), good communication from the company and financial security all cut the odds [144](#cite:144). Forty-one percent of organisations report rising [candidate ghosting](#term:candidate-ghosting) [43](#cite:43), and faster offers are accepted more often with no later penalty [15](#cite:15). A [cleared](#term:security-clearance) opening stretches the interval to the length of the [clearance clock](#term:end-to-end-timeliness), 197 to 243 days on the current figures [126](#cite:126), and a key-personnel hire stretches it to the award date the firm does not set [108](#cite:108).
mechanism: Acceptance is a decision the candidate keeps revisiting while competing offers arrive and finances tighten; every week of delay adds exposure and weakens the links that hold the decision in place [144](#cite:144). The firm controls the interval only where no clearance or award sits inside it ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to_tell: The planned start is more than a few weeks out and depends on an event the firm does not control [144](#cite:144) [126](#cite:126).
The hire has no named contact and no scheduled check-in before the start [144](#cite:144).
The candidate came through a posting rather than a referral and holds competing offers [144](#cite:144).
conflicts: The ghosting rates come from entry-level, customer-facing roles at one telecommunications employer; the mechanism, not the rate, is what transfers to cleared technical hiring [144](#cite:144).

name: Payroll before access is the firm's cost, not the customer's
what: A [time-and-materials](#term:time-and-materials-contract) or labor-hour contract pays fixed hourly rates for labor that meets the category's qualifications and is performed on the contract [98](#cite:98) [99](#cite:99); an employee waiting for a [clearance](#term:security-clearance) or a badge performs none. Labor that cannot be charged to a contract is an [indirect cost](#term:overhead-rate), pooled and spread over the firm's other work through its rates [148](#cite:148). The firm may not [sponsor](#term:clearance-sponsorship) the clearance ahead of a contract need to shorten the wait [119](#cite:119), and whether the hire may do unclassified work on the contract before the clearance arrives depends on the contract's security terms ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker) from [146](#cite:146)).
mechanism: The rate the customer pays assumes productive, qualified hours [98](#cite:98); the wait produces none, so its cost moves into overhead or [G&A](#term:general-and-administrative-rate) and raises the firm's rates on every other contract, which in turn narrows what it can pay (synthesis from [148](#cite:148) and c-salary-above-rate). A small firm with few contracts has a small base to spread it over (synthesis).
how_to_tell: The offer is accepted, the clearance is pending, and no funded task exists for the interval (synthesis).
The firm's indirect rates are set for the year and the [bench payroll](#term:hiring-ahead) was not in them [148](#cite:148) (synthesis).
conflicts: No study of bridge-work practice or its effect on retention through the wait was found; the record rests on the contract and cost rules.

name: The first three days carry statutory clocks the firm cannot move
what: [Section 2 of Form I-9](#term:form-i-9) must be completed within three business days of the day employment begins, on the first day for a job shorter than that, and the employee chooses which documents to show [130](#cite:130). A contractor with the [E-Verify clause](#term:e-verify) initiates verification within three business days of the hire date, must be enrolled within thirty days of award, and verifies staff assigned to the contract within ninety days [128](#cite:128); the clause attaches to contracts over \$150,000 lasting 120 days or more in the United States [129](#cite:129). A [background report](#term:consumer-report) under the [FCRA](#term:fair-credit-reporting-act) needs a stand-alone disclosure and written permission before it is ordered, and a [pre-adverse-action notice](#term:adverse-action-notice) with the report before any decision against the person [136](#cite:136). Criminal-history questions wait until after a conditional offer under the [Fair Chance Act](#term:fair-chance-act), with an exception for [cleared](#term:security-clearance) positions [48](#cite:48), and medical examinations wait until the conditional offer under the ADA [34](#cite:34). [Drug testing](#term:drug-free-workplace) is no longer a DFARS requirement; the clause was reserved in May 2026 [134](#cite:134), leaving the FAR's policy and notification program, which requires no testing [135](#cite:135). A cyber role needs the [foundational qualification](#term:dod-8140) on day one [139](#cite:139).
mechanism: Each check has a legal trigger tied to the start or the offer, and each can surface information that ends the hire: a failed verification, a disputed report, an unmet qualification [128](#cite:128) [136](#cite:136) [139](#cite:139). The sequence matters because a step taken out of order is itself a violation ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker) from [136](#cite:136) and [48](#cite:48)).
how_to_tell: The start date is set but the E-Verify enrollment or the I-9 process has no owner [128](#cite:128) [130](#cite:130).
The background check was ordered on the application form's consent language [136](#cite:136).
The firm tests for drugs under a policy written for the old DFARS clause [134](#cite:134) [135](#cite:135).
conflicts: The Form I-9 Section 1 timing page (by the first day of employment) failed to fetch; Section 2 is cited [130](#cite:130).

name: A foreign national cannot start on controlled or classified work without an authorization
what: Releasing [ITAR technical data](#term:itar) to a foreign person in the United States is itself an export [132](#cite:132), and a [U.S. person](#term:us-person) for that purpose is a permanent resident or a protected individual under the anti-discrimination statute, which reaches nationals, refugees and asylees as well as citizens [133](#cite:133). The employer assesses only the positions that work with controlled items, keeps that assessment apart from the [Form I-9](#term:form-i-9), never tells applicants the export rules require a citizenship, and applies to State or Commerce for an authorization before a non-U.S. person does the work [131](#cite:131). On classified work a non-U.S. citizen can be [cleared](#term:security-clearance) only by a [Limited Access Authorization](#term:limited-access-authorization) in rare cases and never for [Top Secret](#term:top-secret), RD, COMSEC, intelligence or NATO information [119](#cite:119). [Sponsoring](#term:clearance-sponsorship) a worker from abroad on an [H-1B](#term:h-1b) has carried a \$100,000 payment since September 2025, extended for a year on September 21, 2026, though a court vacated the implementing policy in June 2026 and collection is paused [142](#cite:142) [143](#cite:143); a \$103,265 [fee](#term:fee) on cap-subject petitions is proposed [141](#cite:141). Title VII permits refusing a hire for a position subject to a national-security requirement the person does not meet [140](#cite:140).
mechanism: The licence, the clearance and the visa are each decided outside the firm and each takes its own time; the one thing the firm decides, who it tells what and when, is governed by the anti-discrimination rules on the other side [131](#cite:131) [49](#cite:49).
how_to_tell: The position works with ITAR or [EAR](#term:ear) items and the chosen candidate is not a U.S. person under §120.62 [133](#cite:133) [131](#cite:131).
The posting says "U.S. citizens only" and no law or contract requires it [131](#cite:131) [49](#cite:49).
The candidate is outside the United States and would need a new H-1B petition [142](#cite:142).
conflicts: The H-1B payment is extended on paper and unenforced under a court order; the appeal is pending [142](#cite:142) [143](#cite:143).

name: Adjustment is left to the newcomer
what: Whether a new hire settles into the role, the team and the firm is predicted by what the firm does in the first weeks. Across 183 samples, institutionalized [onboarding tactics](#term:socialization-tactics) correlate .24 to .40 with [role clarity](#term:newcomer-adjustment), task mastery, social acceptance and fit, and the social tactics, experienced insiders as guides and affirmation of who the newcomer already is, are the strongest at .29 to .47 [152](#cite:152). Social acceptance then carries the outcomes: .35 with performance, −.27 with [intentions to leave](#term:withdrawal-cognitions) and −.12 with leaving [152](#cite:152). At one firm with no standardized [orientation](#term:onboarding) a quarter of newcomers left within a year; having insiders as role models roughly halved the odds (OR 0.44), as did investiture (OR 0.52) [155](#cite:155). Support from the supervisor and the team falls week by week over the first ninety days, what the newcomer got at the start predicts integration and commitment at ninety days, and a supervisor who undermines triples the hazard of leaving [156](#cite:156).
mechanism: Adjustment runs through three things the newcomer has to acquire, clarity about the role, mastery of the tasks and acceptance by the people, and the firm's tactics and the newcomer's own proactivity are the two sources [152](#cite:152) [153](#cite:153). A small firm with no program leaves the second source to carry the whole load ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to_tell: There is no written first-week, first-month and first-quarter plan and no named insider for the hire [152](#cite:152) (synthesis).
The newcomer is asking peers what the role is at week six [152](#cite:152).
Supervisor contact has thinned since the first week [156](#cite:156).
conflicts: The meta-analytic links from adjustment to actual turnover are small (about −.1); the larger effects are on satisfaction, commitment and performance [152](#cite:152).

name: The ramp to full productivity is longer than the rate assumes
what: Where output can be counted per worker it rose 53 percent in the first year on the job, with a very steep [learning curve](#term:time-to-productivity) and pay profiles much flatter than output in the first eighteen months [157](#cite:157). A labor-category rate assumes qualified, productive hours from the first day [98](#cite:98), and a [time-and-materials contract](#term:time-and-materials-contract) pays only for hours by people who meet the category [99](#cite:99). No public benchmark for the ramp of a technical professional was found; vendor estimates of weeks to full productivity are not carried ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
mechanism: Learning is front-loaded and the people who stay learn fastest [157](#cite:157); the firm bills at a rate that assumes the finished worker while paying for the unfinished one, or bills a lower category and loses margin (synthesis from [98](#cite:98) [157](#cite:157)). Training that does not match the work lengthens the ramp [162](#cite:162).
how_to_tell: The hire is billed at a category whose qualifications they meet on paper but whose output they have not reached (synthesis).
There is no readiness milestone against which the ramp is measured [157](#cite:157) (synthesis).
conflicts: The 53 percent figure is from windshield installers at one company; the shape transfers, the slope does not [157](#cite:157).

name: The customer will not accept, or pay for, a junior in the slot
what: Each [labor category](#term:labor-category) carries qualifications, and hours performed by people who do not meet them are not paid unless the contracting officer authorises a substitution [99](#cite:99) [98](#cite:98). The rule is enforced after the fact: an Inspector General found DoD improperly charged for 101 of 112 contractor employees who did not meet their labor categories, and for 41 more who met the base requirements but lacked relevant education and experience, with potential improper payments of about \$35 million across twelve task orders [173](#cite:173). A cyber work role needs its foundational certificate on the day the work starts [139](#cite:139). Where the customer approves candidates by name, its criteria sit on top of the category (sweep 7).
mechanism: The category is a contract term about the person, not about the output; a junior who could do the work still cannot be billed in the senior slot [99](#cite:99), and a customer that accepted one is the one the audit catches [173](#cite:173) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to_tell: The candidate's résumé does not meet the category's years or [degree line](#term:degree-requirement) [99](#cite:99) [173](#cite:173).
The customer has rejected a submitted résumé or asked for a substitution approval (synthesis).

name: The skills the firm pays for are portable
what: Standard theory says workers pay for [general training](#term:general-human-capital) because they can take it anywhere; the observed fact is that employers pay for it, which the economics explains by the training firm's better knowledge of what the worker can do [161](#cite:161). Training raises output about twice as much as it raises pay (0.6 against 0.3 percent per point of training), so the firm keeps part of the return while the worker stays [159](#cite:159). Tuition reimbursement did raise retention at one establishment, but [four-fifths](#term:four-fifths-rule) of the effect came from who chose to join, not from the people reimbursed [160](#cite:160). A [cleared](#term:security-clearance) and trained professional faces a market that pays a premium and in which 13 percent switched employers for pay in a year [89](#cite:89). [Repayment agreements](#term:training-repayment-agreement) that try to hold the investment are under pressure: nearly 10 percent of workers had one in 2020, the federal consumer regulator treats them as debt [166](#cite:166), California bars most of them for contracts after January 1, 2026 [167](#cite:167), Colorado limits them to distinct training at cost declining over two years [168](#cite:168), and the research the regulator cites puts their effect at about 15 percent less quitting [166](#cite:166).
mechanism: General skills raise the worker's outside value as fast as the inside value; the firm's hold is its information advantage [161](#cite:161), its pay progression (sweep 6), and whatever retention term the law still allows [167](#cite:167) [168](#cite:168) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to_tell: The firm's trained staff leave within a year of a certification or a clearance (synthesis; see c-cleared-supply-scarce).
The training agreement requires repayment of more than the cost, charges interest, or covers required training [166](#cite:166) [168](#cite:168).
Pay has not moved with the new capability [89](#cite:89) (synthesis; sweep 6).
conflicts: The 15 percent quitting effect is research the CFPB cites, not read here (todo); the state rules rest on law-firm summaries pending the statutes in states.yaml [166](#cite:166) [167](#cite:167) [168](#cite:168).

name: Mentoring capacity is the senior staff's billable time
what: Learning from more knowledgeable coworkers is a measurable part of what a job pays, four to nine percent of total compensation on German establishment data [158](#cite:158), and the [social tactics](#term:socialization-tactics) that put insiders beside the [newcomer](#term:newcomer-adjustment) are the strongest [onboarding](#term:onboarding) predictors at r .29 to .47 [152](#cite:152). The hours come from the people the contract bills: a [time-and-materials contract](#term:time-and-materials-contract) pays for qualified hours on contract tasks [99](#cite:99), so [mentoring](#term:mentoring) that is not a task in the statement of work is [indirect cost](#term:overhead-rate) [148](#cite:148), [allowable](#term:allowable-cost) in the rates as job-related training [175](#cite:175) but paid out of margin ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)). The protégé's own measurable gains from mentoring are small [164](#cite:164) [165](#cite:165); the firm's gain is the newcomer's adjustment [152](#cite:152).
mechanism: A small firm has few seniors and each is billable; every mentoring hour is either a contract hour forgone or an indirect hour added to the rates [99](#cite:99) [148](#cite:148); a senior with several trainees at once has less of either (synthesis).
how_to_tell: Mentoring is expected but no hours are allocated and no senior is named [152](#cite:152) (synthesis).
The senior's utilisation target leaves no room for it [99](#cite:99) (synthesis).
Several developmental hires share one senior (synthesis).
conflicts: No study of how many trainees a senior can carry, or of mentoring time budgets, was found.

name: Training that does not look like the work does not transfer
what: Whether a trained skill is used on the job depends on conditions the firm sets more than on the course: a realistic training environment, behavioural modelling and error management in the design, a supervisor who expects the skill to be used (ρ .31 against .14 for peers), a [transfer climate](#term:transfer-of-training) (.37) and an early opportunity to perform [162](#cite:162). Motivation and self-efficacy matter most for open skills, the ones performed differently each time [163](#cite:163). An often-repeated estimate that only a tenth of training spending transfers is a 1982 figure, not a measurement [162](#cite:162). On classified programs the actual material may not be available for training at all ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
mechanism: Transfer is a property of the fit between the practice and the job and of what happens in the weeks after the course [162](#cite:162); a generic certification course followed by months of unrelated work transfers little whatever it cost (synthesis).
how_to_tell: The training is a vendor course with no task from the firm's own work in it [162](#cite:162).
The first chance to use the skill is months after the course [162](#cite:162).
The supervisor has not said what they expect to change [162](#cite:162).
conflicts: The meta-analytic coefficients are carried from a peer-reviewed review of Blume et al. 2010 and Colquitt et al. 2000; the meta-analyses themselves are todos [162](#cite:162).

name: Development runs ahead of a place to use it
what: The rules draw the line at the employee and the contract: training costs for other than bona fide employees are [unallowable](#term:allowable-cost) [175](#cite:175), a [clearance](#term:security-clearance) may not be requested ahead of a contract need [119](#cite:119), and a [SkillBridge](#term:skillbridge) partner commits to offers for 75 percent of completers [74](#cite:74). [Registered Apprenticeship](#term:registered-apprenticeship) adds obligations of its own, and smaller employers told GAO that registration and reporting were especially hard, that cost deterred them, and that 42 percent of participants complete within a year of the expected date [172](#cite:172). Whether the demand the training points at is real is a plan-stage question (sweep 7).
mechanism: A developmental hire is a bet on a future opening; the cost is certain and allowable only within the rules, the opening is not, and the hire's outside value rises as the training proceeds [175](#cite:175) [161](#cite:161) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to_tell: The trainee has no named contract, [labor category](#term:labor-category) or start date at the end of the plan (synthesis).
The program's obligations (offers, reporting) exceed what the firm's pipeline can meet [74](#cite:74) [172](#cite:172).

name: The return on development is not measured, so every departure looks like failure
what: The one federal cost-benefit study of [apprenticeship](#term:registered-apprenticeship) measured the return to participants (completers' career earnings gains of \$240,037) and to society (benefits exceeding costs by more than \$49,000) and nothing on the employer's side [171](#cite:171). The industry-level evidence says training raises output twice as much as pay [159](#cite:159), and the one-establishment evidence says most of a tuition program's retention effect is in who it attracts [160](#cite:160); neither tells a small firm what its own cohort returned. GAO lists cost among the reasons employers do not train through apprenticeship [172](#cite:172).
mechanism: Without a cohort measure of cost, productive service and retention, the firm judges development by its last departure ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)); the economics give the terms to measure, output against pay over tenure [159](#cite:159) [157](#cite:157).
how_to_tell: The firm cannot say what a developmental cohort cost and billed over two years (synthesis).
A single departure ended the program (synthesis).
conflicts: No study of employer-side returns to apprenticeship or in-house development at small firms was found.

name: Pay falls behind what the person can do and what the person next to them gets
what: Pay itself is a modest predictor of quitting (ρ −.17 across 55 studies) and perceived alternatives a stronger one (.23) [178](#cite:178); what moves people is the comparison. At a large retailer the quit response to own pay turned out to be mostly a response to peers' pay, driven by comparisons with higher-paid peers, and separations were insensitive when raises were similar across peers [182](#cite:182). Employees who learn they earn less than their unit's median search for other jobs while those above gain nothing [92](#cite:92); external hires start about 18 percent above internal promotees [93](#cite:93); the [cleared](#term:security-clearance) market pays a premium and 13 percent of its professionals switched employers for pay in a year [89](#cite:89). The firm's room to answer is bounded by the labor-category rate [98](#cite:98) and by what each market-rate hire has already done to the incumbents' comparison point (c-new-hire-pay-compresses-incumbents).
mechanism: Capability grows faster than the rate the person was hired under (c-ramp-to-productivity-exceeds-plan); the outside market prices the new capability and the inside pay does not; the person learns what peers and new hires get and leaves over the gap, not over the level [182](#cite:182) [92](#cite:92) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to_tell: A new hire in the same category was brought in above incumbents without an equity review [93](#cite:93) [92](#cite:92).
Raises have been unequal across peers doing [substantially equal work](#term:equal-pay-act) [182](#cite:182).
The person's market value ([OEWS](#term:oews), cleared comp) has moved and their pay has not [110](#cite:110) [89](#cite:89) (synthesis).
conflicts: The peer-comparison evidence is from low-wage retail [182](#cite:182); the direction, not the magnitude, is carried.

name: A small firm has few steps up, and the obvious step is the wrong one
what: Internal mobility is among the practices most strongly associated with lower [unit turnover](#term:collective-turnover) (ρ −.25 across 82 studies) [181](#cite:181), and a small firm has little of it to offer. The step it does have is often management, and the evidence on that step is unkind: firms promote on current performance, a worker who sells twice as much is about 15 percent more likely to be promoted, and a doubling of a manager's pre-promotion sales corresponds to a 7.5 percent fall in the manager's value added through the team's results [184](#cite:184) [185](#cite:185). Learning from more knowledgeable coworkers is worth four to nine percent of pay [158](#cite:158), which a firm with one senior per specialty cannot offer twice.
mechanism: The person's growth needs a next assignment; the firm's structure offers a title or nothing; the title taken from the best technical contributor removes them from the work they were best at and puts them over a team they may run worse [184](#cite:184) [185](#cite:185) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to_tell: The firm's only growth path is into management, and the last promotion went to the top performer [184](#cite:184).
A productive engineer has had the same scope for two years with no lateral move available [181](#cite:181) (synthesis).
conflicts: The promotion evidence is from sales organisations; whether technical promotion shows the same pattern has not been studied here [184](#cite:184).

name: The employee is run by the customer and forgotten by the firm
what: Commitment (ρ −.29), fit (−.29), satisfaction (−.28), [embeddedness](#term:job-embeddedness) (−.26) and the quality of leadership (−.24) are the cluster of predictors next after wanting to leave and looking [178](#cite:178). At the business-unit level, employee engagement relates to turnover, productivity, profit and customer satisfaction across 7,939 units [183](#cite:183); a supervisor who undermines a [newcomer](#term:newcomer-adjustment) triples the hazard of leaving [156](#cite:156). An employee placed at a customer site works under the customer's manager, for the customer's goals, with the firm present on payday ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)); the work itself may be frustrating, stagnant or poorly run by people the firm does not employ, which is the row's "limited control" trade-off and the condition of the whole pack (synthesis). Stay interviews and recognition programs have no evidence base found; manager check-ins stand on the leadership and engagement [correlations](#term:correlation-coefficient) [178](#cite:178) [183](#cite:183).
mechanism: Attachment forms through relationships, fit and a sense of being seen; off-site work starves all three on the firm's side and leaves the customer's manager to supply or withhold them [178](#cite:178) [156](#cite:156) (synthesis).
how_to_tell: The firm's manager has not spoken with the person about their work this quarter (synthesis).
The person's day-to-day supervisor is the customer's and the firm hears about problems from the customer first (synthesis).
[Turnover intentions](#term:withdrawal-cognitions) or job search, the strongest signals, are being voiced [178](#cite:178).
conflicts: The unit-level engagement evidence is Gallup's own instrument and authors [183](#cite:183); the coefficients are a todo.

name: One vacancy loads the rest, and the load shows up as stress, not hours
what: Stress and exhaustion predict quitting at ρ .21, role conflict and role ambiguity at .15 each, work–life conflict at .19, while hours of workload as such barely register (−.10) [178](#cite:178); at the unit level, staffing levels were not significantly related to [turnover rates](#term:collective-turnover) [181](#cite:181). On a [time-and-materials contract](#term:time-and-materials-contract) a vacancy is unbilled hours [99](#cite:99), and the firm's instinct is to cover them with the people who remain ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)). What the evidence says will follow is not more quitting from more hours but more quitting from the strain, the conflict and the lost boundary between work and home that the covering creates [178](#cite:178).
mechanism: The cover is invisible in a utilisation report and visible in the predictors that matter: exhaustion, conflict between roles, conflict with home [178](#cite:178); a second departure then repeats the cycle (synthesis).
how_to_tell: A vacancy is being covered by the remaining staff with no end date (synthesis).
Role conflict and exhaustion are what the person describes, not the hours [178](#cite:178).
conflicts: Workload's meta-analytic correlation with turnover is small and negative and staffing levels are not significant [178](#cite:178) [181](#cite:181); the row's mechanism is supported through stress and role conflict, not through hours.

name: An onsite, fixed-schedule job competes against arrangements it cannot offer
what: Workers value the option to work from home at about 8 percent of wages and a predictable schedule at about 20 percent [115](#cite:115); working conditions are compensation in their own right [94](#cite:94). Teachers commuting 45 minutes or more were 10 percentage points more likely to transfer than colleagues at the same school commuting five [194](#cite:194). Classified work happens where the classified information is [119](#cite:119), and a customer site has the customer's hours ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)); the competing offer from a remote-friendly employer is priced in the candidate's head at the amenity rate before the salary is compared [115](#cite:115) (synthesis).
mechanism: The amenity the firm cannot supply is worth a fifth of pay to the median worker and more to some; the commute is a daily reminder; the alternative is one job search away [115](#cite:115) [194](#cite:194) [178](#cite:178) (synthesis).
how_to_tell: The role is onsite and fixed-hours by contract and the person's last competing offer was hybrid [115](#cite:115) (synthesis).
The commute to the customer site is long and the site is not negotiable [194](#cite:194) (synthesis).
conflicts: The commute evidence is from teachers in one district [194](#cite:194); the amenity valuations are from a field experiment on call-centre applicants [115](#cite:115).

name: The job ends when the contract does, and the person knows it
what: Wanting to leave is the strongest predictor of leaving (ρ .56) and the alternatives a person sees come next (.23) [178](#cite:178); an employee on a contract with a known end date, a [recompete](#term:recompete) or a protest carries both. The [right of first refusal](#term:nondisplacement) that once attached to a [successor contractor](#term:successor-contractor) is gone: the order behind it was revoked on January 20, 2025 and the rule rescinded on December 22, 2025, and the implementing contract clause had never been issued [186](#cite:186). A firm with 100 or more employees owes 60 days' notice before a [mass layoff](#term:warn-act) at a site [191](#cite:191); a smaller one owes what it promised ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)). Quits ran 1.9 percent a month economy-wide in August 2026 [57](#cite:57).
mechanism: Uncertainty the firm cannot resolve becomes a [withdrawal cognition](#term:withdrawal-cognitions) the person can act on; the honest account of what is known is the only [lever](#term:lever-record) the firm holds, and honesty is the mechanism by which realistic previews lower turnover [13](#cite:13) [178](#cite:178) (synthesis).
how_to_tell: The contract's option year, recompete or protest is public and the firm has said nothing (synthesis).
Job-search behaviour is visible among the people on the ending contract [178](#cite:178).
conflicts: No study of contract-end uncertainty and quitting among contractor staff was found; the record rests on the general predictors and the rules.

name: The prime, the customer or a competitor hires the person the firm trained
what: External hires are paid about 18 percent more than internal promotees for comparable jobs [93](#cite:93), which is the premium a larger employer can put on the firm's trained and [cleared](#term:security-clearance) engineer; 13 percent of [cleared professionals](#term:cleared-population) switched employers for pay in a year [89](#cite:89). The firm cannot agree with the [prime](#term:prime-contractor) or a teammate not to hire each other's people: such agreements are illegal without any showing of harm and may be prosecuted as felonies, and a [non-solicitation term](#term:non-solicitation-agreement) survives only as a collateral and reasonably necessary part of a real collaboration [187](#cite:187); the federal [noncompete](#term:noncompete-agreement) ban is gone and the state rules vary [169](#cite:169). What holds people is what the turnover evidence says holds them: [embeddedness](#term:job-embeddedness) (ρ −.26), commitment, fit and the supervisor [178](#cite:178), and [firm-specific training](#term:specific-human-capital) (−.40 at the unit level) [181](#cite:181).
mechanism: The firm invests, the person's outside value rises [161](#cite:161), and the party with the largest base to spread the premium across can pay it; restrictions on the hiring party are criminal and restrictions on the person are state-limited, so the hold has to be in the job [187](#cite:187) [169](#cite:169) [178](#cite:178) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
how_to_tell: The [subcontract](#term:subcontractor) or [teaming agreement](#term:teaming-agreement) contains a [no-hire term](#term:no-poach-agreement) outside any collaboration scope [187](#cite:187).
The prime has interviewed the firm's onsite staff (synthesis).

name: The knowledge the contract depends on sits with one or two people
what: When a worker dies unexpectedly, the firm raises the pay of the remaining people in the same occupation to keep them, the people in other occupations are worth less without the specialist, and the [replacement cost](#term:replacement-cost) is largest in thin labour markets and for specialised skills [193](#cite:193). At the unit level, turnover lowers customer satisfaction and production efficiency at about −.22 and profit margin at −.15 [181](#cite:181); [firm-specific training](#term:specific-human-capital) is the practice most strongly tied to keeping a unit together (−.40) [181](#cite:181). The ISO human-capital standard names succession metrics among the things a firm should be able to report [46](#cite:46). A small technical firm with one person per specialty is the thin-market, specialised case by construction ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
mechanism: Specialised knowledge is not substitutable at short notice; its holder's departure removes capacity the contract assumed and raises the price of everyone adjacent [193](#cite:193); the only pre-emptive moves are to spread the knowledge and to name the successor [181](#cite:181) [46](#cite:46) (synthesis).
how_to_tell: One person is the only one who can perform a contract task or hold a customer relationship (synthesis).
There is no named successor or documented handoff for the key [labor categories](#term:labor-category) [46](#cite:46) (synthesis).
conflicts: The death-shock evidence is German and economy-wide [193](#cite:193); no study of knowledge concentration in small contractors was found.

name: A departure sets contract and security clocks running
what: A named key person cannot be diverted without the contracting officer's written consent and at least 30 days' notice with a substitute whose skills, experience and credentials meet or exceed the requirement; a resignation on shorter notice must be reported as soon as practicable [188](#cite:188).
