A [cleared](#term:security-clearance) employee's termination is reported to the cognizant security agency, adverse information is reported even after the person has gone, and access ends at once on a denial or revocation [189](#cite:189) [119](#cite:119). A proposed key person who becomes unavailable before award must be reported to the agency at GAO's standard [108](#cite:108). A firm of 100 or more owes 60 days' notice before a qualifying layoff [191](#cite:191).
mechanism: The contract treats the named person as part of the deliverable and the security rules treat them as a reportable event; the firm's obligations run to the customer and the agency before they run to the backfill ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker) from [188](#cite:188) [189](#cite:189)).
how_to_tell: The departing person is named in a contract or a pending proposal [188](#cite:188) [108](#cite:108).
The person holds eligibility [sponsored](#term:clearance-sponsorship) by the firm [189](#cite:189).
conflicts: The key-personnel clause carried is one agency's (HHS); other agencies' notice periods and approval standards differ (todo) [188](#cite:188).

name: An internal move keeps the person and opens a new vacancy with the whole clock
what: Internal mobility is among the practices most strongly associated with lower turnover (ρ −.25) [181](#cite:181), so the move is worth making; it leaves behind a vacancy that carries the full sequence the pack describes, from the posting to the 197-to-243-day [clearance clock](#term:end-to-end-timeliness) [126](#cite:126), and on a contract with named [key personnel](#term:key-personnel-clause) it needs the customer's consent and an [equal-or-better substitute](#term:key-personnel-substitution) first [188](#cite:188). If the move is a promotion decided on current performance, the team left behind may do worse under the new manager [184](#cite:184) [185](#cite:185).
mechanism: The firm trades a departure it cannot control for a vacancy it can plan, at the price of the backfill's lead time and the customer's approval ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker) from [181](#cite:181) [188](#cite:188) [126](#cite:126)).
how_to_tell: A move is being offered to keep someone and no backfill has been started [126](#cite:126) (synthesis).
The person is named in the contract the move takes them off [188](#cite:188).

name: The opening is tentative, unfunded or staffed for a proposal
what: A [clearance](#term:security-clearance) may be requested only for an employee a classified contract needs, never to build a cache [119](#cite:119); an investigation requested before employment needs a written commitment and a start within 45 days of the grant [119](#cite:119). A candidate named in a proposal is hired if the proposal wins and must be reported to the agency if they become unavailable before award [108](#cite:108); naming a person the firm has no reasonable basis to deliver is a misrepresentation that can unwind the award, as it did where a proposed key person had committed elsewhere and said so [203](#cite:203). Recruiting spend before funding is the firm's [indirect cost](#term:overhead-rate) [148](#cite:148), and the interval between an acceptance and a start the firm does not control is the one in which accepted hires disappear [144](#cite:144).
mechanism: The firm recruits against a demand that someone else decides; every rule in the chain, the [sponsorship](#term:clearance-sponsorship) need, the proposal representation, the start date, assumes the demand is real, and the candidate bears the wait ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker) from [119](#cite:119) [203](#cite:203) [144](#cite:144)).
how_to_tell: There is no funded contract, task order or DD 254 behind the [requisition](#term:requisition) [119](#cite:119) (synthesis).
The opening exists because of a proposal, and the candidate's commitment is a contingent offer with no date [108](#cite:108) [203](#cite:203).
Nobody can name the decision authority, the funding line and the start date (synthesis).

name: The requisition describes several jobs as one
what: What a posting draws is set by its title and its pay figure: within a title, more pay draws more applicants, and across titles the applicant pool changes with the word [65](#cite:65). A [labor category](#term:labor-category) carries one set of qualifications and hours by people who do not meet it are not paid [98](#cite:98) [99](#cite:99); a requirement that is not job-related and consistent with business necessity cannot be defended if it has [adverse impact](#term:adverse-impact) [30](#cite:30) [32](#cite:32). A [requisition](#term:requisition) written to cover two roles draws candidates for neither, bills in a category that fits neither, and fails the [job-analysis](#term:job-analysis) test the selection rules assume ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
mechanism: The customer's statement of work describes outcomes; the firm translates it into one person because that is the slot it has; the translation loses the distinction between the deliverables and the competencies that produce them (synthesis from [65](#cite:65) [98](#cite:98)).
how_to_tell: The posting lists two unrelated skill sets as required and the title fits one of them [65](#cite:65).
The labor category's qualification line matches part of the duties [99](#cite:99).
conflicts: No study of multi-role requisitions as such was found; the record rests on the posting evidence and the category rule.

name: Preferences are written as requirements, and nobody can say whose they are
what: Roles dropping [degree requirements](#term:degree-requirement) rose almost fourfold from 2014 to 2023 while hiring without a degree in those roles barely moved, because the screens did not change [68](#cite:68) [58](#cite:58); a degree line narrows the pool (c-degree-requirement- shrinks-pool). A requirement with [adverse impact](#term:adverse-impact) must be job-related and consistent with business necessity [30](#cite:30) [32](#cite:32). In a customer-governed [requisition](#term:requisition) three sources of requirement are mixed, the contract's [labor category](#term:labor-category) [99](#cite:99), the customer's stated preference, and the firm's own, and only the first is enforceable as written; the customer may specify the result and reject the product but may not run the firm's hiring as if the staff were its own [197](#cite:197).
mechanism: A preference inherited from the customer or the last incumbent is written into the posting as a must, the pool shrinks to the people who have it, and no one owns the decision to drop it ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker) from [68](#cite:68) [197](#cite:197)).
how_to_tell: A requirement in the posting cannot be traced to the contract, the customer in writing, or a [job analysis](#term:job-analysis) [32](#cite:32) (synthesis).
The requirement is a degree or years figure the category does not require [99](#cite:99) [68](#cite:68).

name: The firm and the customer mean different things by "qualified"
what: The contract's definition is the [labor category](#term:labor-category)'s education and experience line, which contracting officers are expected to validate by résumé review and which an audit found unvalidated for 1,219 of 1,287 employees and breached for 101 of 112 who did not meet it [173](#cite:173) [99](#cite:99). The evidence's definition is a structured, scored assessment of the work, since [structured interviews](#term:structured-interview) and [work samples](#term:work-sample-test) predict performance and unstructured judgement barely does [1](#cite:1) [7](#cite:7). The customer's definition is whatever its reviewer applies, which the personal-services rule allows to be a specification of the result but not a supervision of the hire [197](#cite:197). Rejections that come back without reasons tied to any of the three cannot be acted on; no study of customer rejection feedback was found ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
mechanism: Three definitions, one of them enforceable, one of them valid and one of them decisive, applied to the same résumé (synthesis from [99](#cite:99) [1](#cite:1) [197](#cite:197)).
how_to_tell: The firm's shortlist is rejected by the customer without reasons tied to the category or a written criterion (synthesis).
The firm and the customer have never reviewed an example profile against the same scorecard (synthesis).
conflicts: The feedback half (B6) is unstudied; the record carries the rules and the selection evidence, not evidence on rejection reasons.

name: The customer's approval has no clock and the candidate does
what: Where the contract gives the customer approval of named staff, the approval is a contract step with no stated period unless the clause gives one; the [key-personnel clause](#term:key-personnel-clause) carried gives the contractor 30 days to propose a substitute but the government no period to answer [188](#cite:188). Candidates leave slow processes: earlier offers were accepted more often with no later penalty [15](#cite:15), and those who withdrew differed in their perceptions of the organisation and the process [16](#cite:16). The customer may specify and reject but may not supervise the hire, which also means the firm cannot compel the decision [197](#cite:197).
mechanism: The firm's clock (the posting, the interview, the offer) runs against the customer's (the review, the badge, the read-in); the candidate experiences their sum and attributes it to the firm ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker) from [15](#cite:15) [16](#cite:16) [188](#cite:188)).
how_to_tell: A submitted résumé has sat with the customer longer than the firm's own decision took (synthesis).
The contract names approval but no review period [188](#cite:188) (synthesis).
conflicts: No study of customer approval cycles was found; the record rests on the withdrawal and speed evidence and the clause.

name: Recruiting spend is visible, vacancy cost and cash exposure are not
what: The median cost of a nonexecutive hire was \$1,200 in 2025 and of an executive hire \$10,625, with agency fees, relocation and recruiter time among the components [196](#cite:196); [sign-on bonuses](#term:signing-bonus) are used by 80 percent of organisations and evaluated by 12 percent [118](#cite:118), and on cost-type work are [allowable](#term:allowable-cost) only under a plan that predates the work [100](#cite:100). The [cost of the vacancy](#term:vacancy-cost) is harder to see: about a fifth of salary per replacement in the case-study median [180](#cite:180), unbilled hours on a [time-and-materials contract](#term:time-and-materials-contract) [99](#cite:99), and at the unit level lower customer satisfaction and productivity (−.22) [181](#cite:181). The cash side is a timing gap: a [proper invoice](#term:prompt-payment) is paid in 30 days by default [202](#cite:202), with a [15-day goal](#term:accelerated-payment) for small business contractors [201](#cite:201), while a hire made ahead of the first invoice is paid from the indirect pools [148](#cite:148).
mechanism: Three numbers decide a [requisition](#term:requisition) and only the first appears on an invoice: the [acquisition spend](#term:cost-per-hire), the vacancy's cost in contribution and delivery, and the cash the firm fronts between payroll and payment ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker) from [196](#cite:196) [180](#cite:180) [202](#cite:202)).
how_to_tell: The firm can state its agency [fee](#term:fee) and not its vacancy cost (synthesis).
A hire is planned against a task order whose first payment is more than two payrolls away [202](#cite:202) (synthesis).
conflicts: No primary on recruiting-agency fee levels was found; the fee is a component in SHRM's cost-per-hire definition and is otherwise vendor-stated [196](#cite:196).

name: Some roles cannot be staffed profitably at the contract's rate
what: A [billing rate](#term:wrap-rate) is built in layers, fringe on labor, [overhead](#term:overhead-rate) on labor and fringe, [general and administrative expense](#term:general-and-administrative-rate) on the whole, profit on top [206](#cite:206), and the labor-category rate it has to fit under was fixed at award [98](#cite:98) with schedule ceilings published [111](#cite:111) and at most three increases a period [117](#cite:117). Market pay for the category is public [110](#cite:110) and rising about 3 percent a year [103](#cite:103); the service-contract floor sits beneath [101](#cite:101). Where the market salary times the firm's layers exceeds the rate, the role loses money at any hire, and the only moves are to redistribute the work, deliver it as a team at mixed categories, or change the rate or the scope, each of which the contract may bar ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker) from [98](#cite:98) [117](#cite:117) [99](#cite:99)).
mechanism: The rate was priced on an assumption about the person; the market moved, or the assumption was wrong; the arithmetic is fixed by the firm's own cost structure and the contract's ceiling (synthesis from [206](#cite:206) [98](#cite:98) [103](#cite:103)).
how_to_tell: The [OEWS](#term:oews) median for the SOC code, loaded at the firm's rates, exceeds the category's ceiling [110](#cite:110) [111](#cite:111) (synthesis).
The role has been open across more than one rate period with no adjustment [117](#cite:117) (synthesis).
conflicts: The rate arithmetic is synthesis from the cost rules; no source states the feasibility test as such.

name: Recruiting starts when the vacancy opens, and every vacancy is treated alike
what: The government's own planning principles ask an organisation to determine the critical skills it will need, tailor strategies to the gaps, build the capability and measure progress [205](#cite:205); a firm that starts at the vacancy has none of that in place and faces a 45-day median fill [43](#cite:43) or a 197-to-243-day [clearance clock](#term:end-to-end-timeliness) [126](#cite:126) from a standing start. Thirty-two percent of small firms report unfilled openings and 87 percent of those hiring report few or no qualified applicants [71](#cite:71); openings ran at 4.3 percent of employment economy-wide in August 2026 [57](#cite:57). Vacancies differ in what they cost, in contribution, in delivery and in the strain on the people covering them [180](#cite:180) [181](#cite:181) [178](#cite:178), and a firm that ranks none of them ranks them by whoever shouts ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
mechanism: [Forecasting](#term:demand-forecast) is guidance, not evidence; its absence is measurable in the lead time lost against the [clearance](#term:security-clearance) and hiring clocks and in the undifferentiated attention given to openings of different value (synthesis from [205](#cite:205) [126](#cite:126) [181](#cite:181)).
how_to_tell: The firm has no rolling list of expected openings with dates and categories [205](#cite:205) (synthesis).
Every open [requisition](#term:requisition) has the same owner and the same priority (synthesis).
conflicts: No study of forecast accuracy or of vacancy prioritisation in small contractors was found; the record rests on guidance and on the clocks.

name: Partner support is capped, consented and competitively constrained
what: On a [set-aside](#term:set-aside) services contract the [prime](#term:prime-contractor) may pay no more than half the amount paid by the government to [subcontractors](#term:subcontractor) that are not [similarly situated](#term:limitations-on-subcontracting), measured by the end of each period [198](#cite:198). Without an [approved purchasing system](#term:consent-to-subcontract), any cost-type, [time-and-materials](#term:time-and-materials-contract) or labor-hour subcontract needs the contracting officer's advance consent with the subcontractor named and priced, and consent transfers no responsibility [199](#cite:199). Subcontractor labor bills at its own category rates where not competitively awarded [98](#cite:98). The firm and the partner may not agree not to hire each other's people; a [non-solicitation term](#term:non-solicitation-agreement) survives only inside the collaboration [187](#cite:187).
mechanism: The gap a partner could fill is bounded by a percentage, an approval and an antitrust line, and the partner's staff remain the partner's to move ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker) from [198](#cite:198) [199](#cite:199) [187](#cite:187)).
how_to_tell: The subcontracted share of a set-aside is approaching half the amount paid [198](#cite:198).
A partner's people are on the contract without the contracting officer's consent [199](#cite:199).

name: Staffing decisions run on anecdote because the records are not kept
what: Nearly a thousand HR professionals disagreed with what the selection research had found, most of all on the predictors that matter most [204](#cite:204). The records that would replace anecdote are partly required by law: application and [selection records](#term:applicant-record-retention) for a year from the decision [200](#cite:200), applicant-flow records by race, sex and ethnic group for the [adverse-impact](#term:adverse-impact) computation [31](#cite:31), and four years under California's automated-decision rules [40](#cite:40); the [Internet Applicant rule](#term:executive-order-11246)'s contractor-specific record duty goes with the EO 11246 regulations on October 26, 2026 [86](#cite:86). The human-capital reporting standard names [cost per hire](#term:cost-per-hire), quality of hire and succession among the metrics a firm should be able to state [46](#cite:46); small firms run a median of six [requisitions](#term:requisition) per recruiter [196](#cite:196).
mechanism: Without a record of where candidates stopped and why, the firm reasons from the last case; the law already requires most of the record, so the cost of keeping it is the discipline, not the data ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker) from [204](#cite:204) [200](#cite:200) [31](#cite:31)).
how_to_tell: The firm cannot say at which stage its last ten candidates were lost and why (synthesis).
Application records are discarded at the close of a requisition [200](#cite:200).

name: Nobody owns the requisition from opening to start
what: Earlier offers are accepted more often with no later penalty [15](#cite:15), candidates who withdraw differ in how they perceived the process [16](#cite:16), and each week between acceptance and start raises the odds the hire never arrives [144](#cite:144); every one of those clocks has steps spread across the firm, the customer and the security office. Small organisations run a median of six [requisitions](#term:requisition) per recruiter [196](#cite:196). Whether a single [accountable owner](#term:requisition-owner) shortens the clocks has not been studied; the record carries the consequences of the delay, not the mechanism ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker)).
mechanism: Steps without an owner wait for the next meeting; the candidate counts the days (synthesis from [15](#cite:15) [144](#cite:144)).
how_to_tell: The requisition has a hiring manager, a recruiter, a contracts lead and a security officer and no one who can say where it stands today (synthesis).
conflicts: The ownership mechanism is unstudied; the evidence is on the delays it is meant to prevent.
